$comment: Where the job queue keeps its state on the broker: the names and subjects every implementation of the queue must use, so that work queued by one survives a switch to another. The queue is JetStream. A job is published once, when it is created, on `<subjectRoot>.<jobType>` into the work-queue stream `stream.name`, which captures every subject under the root; the durable consumer `consumer.durableName` delivers each message to the dispatcher that holds it as the job's lease. The job itself lives in the KV bucket `bucket.name`, one JobRecord per job keyed by the job's id, and every change to a record is a compare-and-swap on its revision. The stream is a work queue; the consumer acknowledges explicitly, delivers from the start, and never gives a message up on its own count (the queue decides retries); the bucket keeps one revision per key. The dispatcher creates the stream, the consumer and the bucket when they are missing and never updates them, so a changed setting takes effect only on a broker that has not seen them. The consumer's name predates the dispatcher and is kept because it is the name on every deployed broker.
